Why defect 1 was a correctness bug, not a match-rate bug.
Defects 2 and 3 only ever produce false NEGATIVES: a real match fails to happen, and the row is correctly reported as unmatched, visible, and auditable (per

's contract that unmatched rows are kept, never dropped). Defect 1 is different in kind — it produces a false POSITIVE that is invisible at the geocoding layer. "77 Burlington Street East" and "77 Burlington Street West" are two different buildings roughly two kilometres apart in Hamilton's lower city, but before this fix they keyed to the exact same anchor, so ANY address-bearing record naming one would silently geocode — successfully, with a matched status and a real lon/lat — to the other's location. A 100% "match" for such a row is wrong, not merely unconfirmed. Because the geocoder has no way to know two different real places were asked for and one anchor was returned, this class of error cannot be caught by a rate measurement at all: the row shows up as "matched," inflating confidence in exactly the join that the whole atlas depends on, while quietly misplacing evidence on the map. That is why it is graded the most serious of the three: defects 2 and 3 hide evidence, lose only true; defect 1 also hides a wrong location behind an apparently successful match.

The anchor-count rise from 349,260 to 354,601 is the direct, expected fingerprint of this fix: previously-collapsed E/W/N/S street pairs now resolve to the distinct places they always were, so the "correct" anchor count was always higher than what was measured under the original design — the earlier number was not merely conservative, it undercounted the true number of distinct addressable places in the study area by conflating some of them.
The jump in geocoding rate on the vacant registry (0.0% -> 32.1% -> 86.9%) tracks the three fixes but should not be read as "defect 1 tripled the rate" — the registry's 84
), so most of the jump from 32.1% to 86.9% is defects 1+2 acting together (a directional street cannot match at all until both the anchor carries its direction AND

can parse a directional query string), while the jump from 0.0% to 32.1% was defect 3 alone (documented already in §19). No single one of the three fixes could have been skipped and still reached 86.9%: dropping the direction fix leaves directional streets permanently unmatchable regardless of municipality handling, and dropping the municipality fix leaves every Hamilton row unmatched regardless of street handling.
§21 Correction to §20: the Burlington Street distance was wrong

§20's Interpretation section states that "77 Burlington Street East" and "77 Burlington Street West" are "two different buildings roughly two kilometres apart in Hamilton's lower city." That figure was not computed — it was an eyeballed guess. It is wrong.
